articleTitle: TENDRA-a simulation tool for the analysis of transport networks employing distributed restoration algorithms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Resilience in Optical Networks
abstract: The distributed, asynchronous nature of self-healing network (SHN) protocols generally renders them intractable to evaluation by analytical methods. Consequently, simulation techniques must be adopted. The authors describe TENDRA (Tool for Evaluation of Network Distributed Restoration Algorithms), a research tool developed to investigate the potential for SHN techniques within the future BT transport network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical protection switches for resilient networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Resilience in Optical Networks
abstract: The authors review the technologies available for optical switching, and relate them to a range of approaches to network resilience including automatic transmission protection, terminal bypass in multi-GHz LANs and switched networks employing separate wavelengths to monitor the condition of the optical plant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Single-moment analysis of unreliable trunk networks employing K-shortest-path routing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Resilience in Optical Networks
abstract: An extension to the MKV GOS method, which was originally limited to OOC-SF (originating office control with spill-forward) table-based routing, is described. This extension allows the analysis of networks employing two additional types of routing, K-shortest-disjoint-loopless-path and K-shortest-loopless path. The extended method is then demonstrated by comparing results for the two K-shortest-path routing types in terms of their overall network grade of service for an example network. In addition, the execution time of the method for a series of networks of increasing size is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
